EmailTemplate.subject: Thank you for your interest in Forensics at ASU
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Dear Future Sun Devil,
Thank you for expressing interest in the Forensics (BS) (https://newcollege.asu.edu/forensics-science-degree) program at Arizona State University. It is the study and application of scientific methods to matters of law. It emphasizes laboratory course work in chemistry and biology, as both areas provide essential experience with techniques commonly used in crime labs. If pursuing a career as a forensic DNA analyst, nine cumulative hours of course work in biochemistry, molecular biology and genetics is required; course work in population genetics is desirable. Students usually look to work as Forensic Science Techs, Pathologists, Medical Scientists, Chemists, and Biological Technicians among many others. By viewing the major map (https://webapp4.asu.edu/programs/t5/roadmaps/ASU00/ASFOREBS/null/ALL/2016), you can see the degree requirements outlined for graduation.
Be sure to review our admission and application requirements (https://students.asu.edu/freshman/requirements) for more information about the application process in an easy to follow format. For finding more ways to pay for college, please visit our scholarships page (https://newcollege.asu.edu/college-scholarships).
It's important to find the right fit for your undergraduate program. A great way to learn more about this degree is to register for one of our upcoming information sessions. You can visit ASU and register for a tour (https://visit.asu.edu/).
We can’t wait to see you here at West campus! If you have any questions about New College, West campus, or one of our 35 programs, please contact our Recruitment Office through the information listed below. Thank you, and we’ll talk to you soon!
Kindest Regards, New College Recruitment Team New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences Arizona State University, West campus asknewcollege@asu.edu 602-543-2890 {!Case.Thread_Id}
